facts.statement: Westphaliasaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur.
An amateur paleontologist named Sönke Simonsen discovered the fossils in 2007.
facts.quote: It was found by Sönke Simonsen, an amateur paleontologist, in 2007

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Höxter district near Bielefeld in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
facts.quote: from the Höxter district near Bielefeld, in the east of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany

facts.statement: The known remains consist of a nearly complete, articulated skeleton that lacks the skull and approximately 38% of the upper neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: It is known from a nearly complete and articulated skeleton missing the skull and about 38% of the upper neck vertebrae

facts.statement: Leonie Schwermann and Martin Sander first named the genus in 2011.
facts.quote: first named by Leonie Schwermann and Martin Sander in 2011

facts.statement: Estimates suggest the animal was about 4.5 meters long.
facts.quote: Estimates suggest that it was about 4.5 m long

facts.statement: Westphaliasaurus belongs to the family Plesiosauridae.
The animal lived during the Lower Jurassic (Pliensbachian stage) in Westphalia, northwestern Germany.
facts.quote: from Lower Jurassic (Pliensbachian stage) deposits of Westphalia, northwestern Germany

facts.statement: Westphaliasaurus lived between 192.9 and 184.2 million years ago during the Pliensbachian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Pliensbachian to Pliensbachian (192.9 to 184.2 million years ago)
